questions.q: What real, relatable comparison does this lesson use to explain an English auction?
options: An eBay listing — each new bid must be higher than the last
A garage sale with fixed prices
A Dutch auction, where prices decrease over time
A lottery with random winners
questions.explain: The lesson directly compares an English auction to an eBay listing: bidders take turns placing higher and higher bids until time runs out.

questions.q: What does the constructor's `nft = IERC721(_nft);` line actually do?
options: References an existing, separately deployed NFT contract so this auction can manage bidding on one of its tokens
Creates and deploys a brand-new NFT contract
Mints a new NFT directly inside the auction contract
Has no real effect on the contract's behavior
questions.explain: The auction contract doesn't create NFTs itself — it references an existing IERC721 contract so it can call functions like transferFrom on a specific token.

questions.q: What two real checks does `start()` perform before doing anything else?
options: That the auction hasn't already started, and that the caller is actually the seller
That the highest bid is nonzero, and that 7 days have passed
That the NFT contract address is valid, and that gas is sufficient
No checks are performed before start() runs
questions.explain: require(!started, "started") and require(msg.sender == seller, "not seller") both run before the function does anything else.

options: To move the NFT into the auction contract's own custody, since it must hold the token to hand it to the eventual winner
To immediately transfer the NFT to the highest bidder
To burn the NFT permanently
This line has no real effect on the NFT's ownership
questions.explain: The auction contract needs to actually hold the NFT (escrow) so it can later transfer it to whoever wins, once the auction ends.

questions.q: According to the real rules stated at the start of this lesson, how long does the auction last once started?
options: 7 days
24 hours
30 days
It never ends automatically
questions.explain: The real rule set by the contract states the auction lasts for 7 days, confirmed later in the code by `endAt = block.timestamp + 7 days;`.
